9-
10:This addendum holds the depth behind [prd.md](prd.md) that does not belong in its main narrative: options considered, constraints for architecture, the reaction contract, UX notes, traceability, and the changes this PRD makes to the brief and the intent. The brief's [addendum](../../briefs/brief-tamagai-2026-09-29/addendum.md) stays the authority for economics (its §1.2); PRD §9 is the claims register of record and supersedes the brief addendum's §1.5. The working files behind this run are in the same folder: `digests/` for the source extracts, and `review-*.md`, `reconcile-*.md`, and `fix-plan.md` for the review trail, which cites draft-1 IDs (mapped in Appendix A).

21-## 1. Decisions made in this PRD run
22-
23-The brief left these decisions to the PRD, or the reviews reopened them. Each one was decided autonomously, and the product owner can overturn any of them. The full log is in `.memlog.md`.
24-
25-### 1.1 Tiers and devices
26-
27-| Decision | Chosen | Alternatives considered | Why |
28-|---|---|---|---|
29-| If on-device speech recognition doesn't fit on 8 GB phones | 8 GB phones move to the server tier; the on-device tier needs the 12 GB class | Gemma's built-in audio on 8 GB phones | Built-in audio misheard 60–75% of words |
30-| Tier before purchase | A small built-in GPU test decides the tier before purchase | Check only after the download | The tier shown at purchase is the tier the family gets |
31-| Downgrade after memory kills | Only foreground kills during a visit count, 2 within 7 days; the device never moves to the server tier on its own | Any low-memory exit | Background kills are routine and would demote paying families |
32-| Model delivery | Our own storage, not Play's on-device AI packs | AI packs | They are in beta, capped at 1.5 GB per pack, and have no purchase gating |
33-
34-### 1.2 Pet life and teaching
35-
36-| Decision | Chosen | Alternatives considered | Why |
37-|---|---|---|---|
38-| The vocabulary limit during teaching | One exception: the single candidate word inside a confirmation | No exception | Without it, teaching is impossible and store claim 1 is false |
39-| Show-and-tell | An on-device image recognizer over the prop set, on every tier | The brain's vision; server upload with a face check | No child images ever leave the device; a smaller, testable label space |
40-| Dream timing | Dream cloud at the first visit of the day | The next visit after charging | No night work, so charging no longer matters; one rule |
41-| Line length | Taught words per line grow with the ladder (1, then 2 at 10 taught words, then 4 at 20), and so do total words per line (2, 3, then 4) | 1–4 words from the start; starter words filling freely | Gives the step at 10 words a real payoff, and keeps early lines safe |
42-| Taught words that look like names | Sent to the server as placeholders; two-word names blocked | Send as vocabulary | A first and last name is personal information |
43-| Voice-teach alternative (NFR-13) | Tap-teach: the same progress, not the same words; family and made-up words need speech | A typed-word teach path | Early readers aged 6–9 can't type reliably, and typed teaching would be a new feature; the brief's rule (every voice action has a tap alternative) still holds |
44-
45-### 1.3 Talk and the brain
46-
47-| Decision | Chosen | Alternatives considered | Why |
48-|---|---|---|---|
49-| When the reaction clock starts | When the microphone closes | At the ear tap; at the first model token | It is the moment the child perceives as "I finished talking", and it is comparable across tiers |
50-| On-device latency | Visible response within 2 s everywhere; brain reaction within 4 s on the on-device tier, bridged by waiting reactions | 2 s everywhere | On-device voice turns were measured at 2.9–3.9 s; an unreachable latency gate would block early access forever |
51-| Reaction timers | Waiting reaction at 2 s, fallback reaction at 6 s, late answers not played but still crisis-checked (FR-52) | One timeout | A designed wait instead of a spinner; 6 s matches the outage rule (FR-92) |
52-| Why a language model at all | Keep decision D1; test talk-lite as a challenger (OQ-18) | Cut the language model | D1 is the product owner's decision; the challenger gets a fair spike |
53-| Crisis evidence precedence | Recognized text and any readable crisis flag are checked before, and regardless of, reaction validation, for every result that arrives within the visit | Discard late or invalid answers whole | The PRD §6.1 hard limit: crisis statements reach the helpline screen whenever there is recognized text or a crisis flag to check |
54-| Visit context | Pip's three previous reactions (IDs) plus interests and scene; never the child's words; cleared after a helpline screen | The child's last three turns | Keeps "nothing kept" true and stops a crisis statement from being resent |

56-### 1.4 Safety and transparency
57-
58-| Decision | Chosen | Alternatives considered | Why |
59-|---|---|---|---|
60-| Helpline screen exits | "Back to Pip" after the narration; the parent gate is never involved; no trace anywhere | Closing only through the parent gate; an adult summary card | Avoids trapping the child and avoids a parent notice under §21812.5 (CQ-23) |
61-| The grown-ups sign | "…how long you play, what you do with Pip, and the words you teach Pip. They can't hear what you say to Pip." | "…not what you say" | Parents see visits, care actions, keepsakes, and word cards, so the old sign was false |
62-| Parent list of Pip's recent lines | Dropped; reports come only from the child's flags | Keep a list of the last 20 lines | Restores "never transcripts" and removes the trace risk |
63-| Flag retention | 7 days on the device | Until reviewed | Long enough for a weekly look, short enough to keep little data |
64-| Crisis test audio | Adult actors, child-voice actors, and synthetic voices only | Research-panel children | Asking a child to record crisis phrases is a safeguarding harm |

66-### 1.5 Parent controls and limits
67-
68-| Decision | Chosen | Alternatives considered | Why |
69-|---|---|---|---|
70-| The care letter on the server tier | Tap-only interests from the interest catalog; the spoken letter only on the on-device tier, processed there | Upload with scrubbing; explicit Art. 9 consent | Parents would mention allergies and religion; nothing sensitive should reach the server |
71-| Caps | Play time separated by less than 15 minutes is one visit, whatever paused it; play time uses a clock that ignores device time changes; after any cap, switching profiles needs the parent gate | A visit ends at goodbye, nap, or app close | Closes the reopen, goodbye, clock-change, and sibling bypasses |
72-| Tightening and loosening limits | Any parent can tighten; any parent with the PIN can relax within the defaults; going beyond the SB 1119 defaults needs a linked parent and the PIN (FR-69) | Every change needs linking | Tightening is always safe; the law restricts loosening |
73-| The allergen list | The union of the US (9) and UK (14) lists, with local names; one-tap "No food allergies" | The US list only | UK families would miss celery, mustard, lupin, molluscs, and sulphites |
74-| Toilet words | A "silly words" category, blocked unless a parent allows it | Always banned; always allowed | Children love them; parents differ |
75-| Parent gate | Parent PIN, masked; strong biometrics only, with a warning; parent PIN always needed to loosen, delete, or buy | Math challenge; device PIN | Children solve math gates, and on a hand-me-down phone the child may know the device PIN |
76-| Parent gate lockouts | 1 minute after 3 wrong PINs, then longer | No lockout | Slows guessing without locking parents out |
77-| Forgotten PIN | An email code for linked parents who opted in to emails; otherwise a 24-hour delayed reset that grants authority within the defaults only; going beyond the defaults again needs a code the linked parent requests in the parent area and receives by email | A time-only reset with full authority; accounts | Elapsed time alone must not confer verified-parent authority (SB 1119). Accepted residual risk: after an unnoticed delayed reset and the 72-hour hold, a child could remove food rules, lift a Pause, or move bedtime later, all within the defaults; NFR-17 playtests watch for it |

79-### 1.6 Unlock and server tier
80-
81-| Decision | Chosen | Alternatives considered | Why |
82-|---|---|---|---|
83-| The free pet | Tap-teach, word cards, ladder, keepsakes, and dreams are free | Teaching only after the unlock | A free pet that never grows loses families before a parent sees the demo, and tying growth to purchase risks SB 1119's relationship-purchase rule |
84-| Route to the offer | One parent-only pointer at the end of essentials, plus a demo tile in the parent area | The offer at the end of essentials; nothing | The pointer carries no price and no urgency, so it fits "no pressure" |
85-| Identifying server calls | A rotating anonymous server credential issued against the purchase and a consent receipt; talk allowance counted on the device; rate ceiling on the server (mechanism: §2.11) | Device ID; purchase token on every call; revocation only when the credential expires | Minimal identifiers, and revocation from the web within 60 s |
86-| Order of operations on the server tier | Notice, then consent, then purchase | Purchase first | No family pays for talk it cannot use (brief addendum §1.3) |
87-| Guarantee economics | The 2× yearly extension rule restored; server-tier sales stop with fewer than 12 months left; guaranteed date on the store listing | The draft-1 terms, unchanged | A late buyer should not pay full price for two months of talk |
88-| Offline unlock after a refund | Removed at the next online check; an offline device keeps it | A 30-day re-verification lease | A lease would break "works in airplane mode"; the revenue leak is small |
89-| Cleanup bound | 10 s after the answer, cancellation, or failure, and 30 s after arrival at most | 10 s after the answer only | A canceled or hung request would otherwise have no deadline |
90-| Consent notice | Covers incidental sensitive data in the child's speech, with explicit consent | Rely on the care letter being tap-only | Children say anything; Art. 9 needs a basis |
91-| Daily-active count boundary | The marker and the total both use the UTC day | A marker per child's day, totaled per UTC day | Mixed boundaries count a child twice, or miss them, around UTC midnight, which falls in US evening play time; the GPU trigger (NFR-9) needs unique children per day |

95-| Decision | Chosen | Alternatives considered | Why |
96-|---|---|---|---|
97-| Counters | Off by default, offered once; the early-access agreement turns them on | On by default | The brief says the parent decides what leaves the device; UK Children's Code standard 7 |
98-| Demo-to-unlock measurement | Two one-time reports per device: the first demo completion, and an unlock within 30 days of it, tagged with the completion week. Each is reported in the counters of the week it happens. A device with no unlock report counts as not buying | Play Console totals divided by counter completions; one yes-or-no report when the 30-day window closes | Play Console totals and counter completions come from different populations; SM-10 needs one. A report at day 30 never arrives from devices that are removed, or whose counters are turned off, before then. Most of those devices did not buy, so a report at day 30 would overstate conversion. Counted like SM-1 |
99-| Helpline referral count | Monthly from US devices with talk, including zeros, fixed size | Only when non-zero; every country | A non-zero-only message would reveal a crisis; the duty is Californian |

234:## 3. The reaction contract
235-
236-This contract answers intent open question #15. Both brains implement one interface; the architecture document confirms the details.
237-- **Request:** the visit context (the prompt card, Pip's vocabulary, the child's interests as catalog IDs, objects on screen, the current wish, the age band, and Pip's three previous reactions), plus the input: audio on the server tier, or the transcript from the on-device recognizer on the on-device tier. On the server tier, the request represents the prompt card by its version reference, and the envelope also carries the server credential, the contract version as protocol metadata, and the first-turn-today marker (FR-90).
238-- **Response:** one schema-validated event from the brain, with these fields. On the server tier, the response envelope also carries `transcript` (text, never persisted), which the server adds outside the brain's generated JSON, so a brain failure never hides it.
239-
240-  | Field | Type or values | Notes |
241-  |---|---|---|
242-  | `emotion` | Enum | — |
243-  | `action` | Enum, with an optional target object ID | — |
244-  | `line` | Text | Optional |
245-  | `unsure` | Boolean | — |
246-  | `crisis` | `none`, `self_harm`, `suicide`, `abuse`, `danger` | — |
247-  | `intent` | `normal`, `out_of_scope`, `health_question`, `self_claim_question`, `affection`, `feeling_stated`, `teach`, `food_or_hazard` | — |
248-  | `proposed_word` | Text | For voice-teach |
249-
250-  There is no field for the child's emotion (FR-49).
251-- **Mechanism:** JSON-schema-constrained output on every runtime: LiteRT-LM `ResponseFormat.json(schema)`; llama.cpp `response_format` or GBNF; vLLM structured outputs. Native tool calls are not used: Gemma 4's tool syntax is not JSON, and vLLM does not enforce required calls.
252-- **Client validator:** it validates the response and converts types (vLLM may return numbers as strings), strips code fences (the 12B wrapped JSON in them), and maps anything unknown to a fallback reaction (FR-43). It checks `transcript` and `crisis` before it validates the reaction, and a reaction's failure never drops them (FR-52). `crisis` is the first field the brain generates, so an answer cut off at the token cap still carries it; an unreadable or unknown value leaves the decision to the phrase list.
253-- **Prompt budget:** a prompt card of about 150 tokens; about 1,500 input tokens per turn, mostly a shared prefix; at most 60 output tokens.
254-- **Placeholders:** the child's name and Pip's name travel as placeholders and are filled in on the device (FR-90).
255-- **The engine, not the prompt,** enforces every hard limit. In the spike, the model often exceeded a 12-word line cap written into the prompt.
256-- **Evaluation suite (FR-51, NFR-14):**
257-  - contract tests against LiteRT-LM, llama.cpp, and vLLM;
258-  - the probe sets listed in NFR-14;
259-  - the crisis set and the child-exaggeration set, run as text and as audio;
260-  - a prosody probe;
261-  - latency measured on the reference devices.

item.text:
§3, **“The reaction contract,”** defines one interface for both brains, resolving intent open question #15; architecture confirms the details.

The **request** contains the prompt card, Pip’s vocabulary, interest catalog IDs, screen objects, current wish, age band, Pip’s three previous reactions, and either server-tier audio or an on-device transcript; server requests also carry the prompt-card version reference, credential, contract version, and first-turn-today marker.

The **response** is one schema-validated event with these fields, plus a server-added, never-persisted `transcript` outside the brain’s JSON so brain failures cannot hide it; there is no child-emotion field.

| Field | Type or values |
|---|---|
| `emotion` | Enum |
| `action` | Enum; optional target object ID |
| `line` | Optional text |
| `unsure` | Boolean |
| `crisis` | `none`, `self_harm`, `suicide`, `abuse`, `danger` |
| `intent` | `normal`, `out_of_scope`, `health_question`, `self_claim_question`, `affection`, `feeling_stated`, `teach`, `food_or_hazard` |
| `proposed_word` | Text for voice-teach |

**Output and validation:** use JSON-schema-constrained output through LiteRT-LM `ResponseFormat.json(schema)`, llama.cpp `response_format` or GBNF, and vLLM structured outputs, without native tool calls; the client converts types, strips code fences, maps unknown reactions to fallback, and checks transcript/crisis before reaction validation, with `crisis` generated first and unreadable or unknown values deferred to the phrase list.

**Limits:** approximately 150 prompt-card tokens, 1,500 input tokens per turn, and at most 60 output tokens; child/Pip names use device-filled placeholders, and the engine enforces every hard limit.

**Evaluation:** contract tests across all three runtimes, NFR-14 probe sets, crisis and child-exaggeration sets as text and audio, a prosody probe, and reference-device latency measurements.
